title: Call Us Navigation
description:
The header's contact-number disclosure — live's `li.call-cta.dropdown` in the Top Menu Right nav. A `core/navigation` carrying one `ollie/mega-menu` whose `menuSlug` is the `dropdown-call-us` template part, so the four numbers stay in the one file the footer and the safari expert panel also read.

## Why this is a navigation and not the accordion

It was a `core/accordion` carrying `is-style-call-us-dropdown` until 2026-08-27. Zared's call, taken from ATI Holidays where the same widget is an Ollie dropdown: hover-open, and far less CSS to make it overlay.

The accordion could not open on hover — `core/accordion`'s Interactivity module binds click and nothing else — and everything that made it *look* like a menu had to be authored against markup that was still, underneath, an in-flow disclosure. Four of those costs are gone outright here, and they are worth naming because each was a bug that shipped:

- **The pop-out is the plugin's own construction.** `ollie/mega-menu` renders its panel in a `__menu-container` that its stylesheet already sets `position: absolute` on. The accordion's panel was a flow child of the accordion item, so theme.json's global block gap reached it as `:root :where(.is-layout-flow) > * { margin-block-start: … }`, and a margin on an absolutely positioned box is added to its inset — the panel hung ~50px low, detached from its trigger.
- **No `hidden="until-found"`.** Core closes an accordion panel with a value that means `content-visibility`, not `display`, so the closed panel's ground, border, radius and shadow went on rendering as a white bar under the trigger. Ollie closes with `opacity` and `visibility` in its own stylesheet, so there is nothing to correct.
- **No pre-hydration flash.** `core/accordion` ships its panel *open* — `accordion-item.php` registers only `isOpen`, `isHidden` is derived in JS, so the server-side directive processor leaves the attribute off and the panel closes when the module hydrates (about a second on dev). Ollie's resting state is CSS, so the panel is shut on first paint with no JavaScript at all.
- **No hand-drawn caret.** Ollie's toggle ships a chevron that rotates off `aria-expanded`, which is the same state a screen reader is announcing. `is-style-main-navigation` hides it, because live's primary nav has no chevrons; live's Call Us *does* have one, so it is kept here.

What it costs: the trigger's label is a block *attribute* (`label`), so it cannot carry an `esc_html_e()` call the way the accordion's inner text could — it is written inline in `patterns/header.php` as an escaped attribute instead. And the disclosure is now a second `<nav>` landmark in the header, which is why the block sets `ariaLabel`.

The safari expert panel keeps the accordion. `ollie/mega-menu` declares `"parent": ["core/navigation"]`, so using it there would put a navigation landmark inside a per-post content panel — wrong for an in-flow disclosure that has no menu semantics. → styles/blocks/accordion/call-us-dropdown.json

## Positioning is CSS here, as it is for the mega menus

Ollie positions its panels from JavaScript, and it does so at `window.load` — measured at 7.8s on dev. assets/styles/ollie-mega-menu.css already documents that at length for the mega-menu panels and overrides it; the same reasoning applies here, and the same remedy. `adjustMegaMenu()` still runs and still writes inline `top`/`left`/`width`/`max-width`; an `!important` author declaration outranks a normal inline style, so those writes land and have no effect.

That is why `position`, the insets, `width` and `max-width` are marked. It is also why the block sets `width: "custom"` rather than `"content"`: `menu-width-content` carries a plugin rule forcing `width: var(--wp--style--global--content-size)`, which is the whole content column for a panel holding four phone numbers. `menu-width-custom` has no plugin stylesheet rule at all — the width is JS-only — so the CSS below is uncontested and `customWidth` exists purely as the editor-visible intent.

`inset-inline: auto 0` anchors the panel to its trigger's inline end, because Call Us sits in a right-aligned utility cluster where a start-aligned panel would run past the content edge. Logical properties, so it flips under RTL for free. The containing block is the item's own `<li>` — core's navigation stylesheet puts `position: relative` on it, and unlike the mega-menu panels this one *wants* that, so none of the `position: static` unpicking in ollie-mega-menu.css applies here.

`topSpacing: 8` matches the 8px in `inset-block-start`. The attribute no longer places anything, but Ollie still reads it for its hover-out grace period (`dynamicHoverDelay` in view.js), so the pointer gets time to cross the gap.

## Scoping

Every selector is scoped to this variation so nothing reaches `is-style-main-navigation`, which shares both the header and the `ollie/mega-menu` class names. Note that an *uncontrolled* navigation — inner blocks in the pattern, no `ref` — puts the variation class on the `<ul>` as well as the `<nav>`, so `.wp-block-navigation.is-style-call-us-navigation` matches twice. Every rule here is idempotent, so that is harmless, but do not write a rule whose effect compounds.

`!important` throughout the `css` field, for the reason main-navigation.json records: WordPress wraps a block style's `css` in `:root :where()` at specificity (0,1,0), which loses to core's own navigation rules — including an always-on `color: inherit` reset — and to Ollie's `.wp-block-navigation .wp-block-ollie-mega-menu__menu-container.menu-justified-*` at (0,3,0).

## Not here

Hover and focus colour, the row hairlines and their tint, the stretched row link, reduced motion and the narrow-viewport fallback are all in assets/styles/ollie-mega-menu.css. The `css` field cannot hold any of them: it strips `:hover` and `:focus-within`, mangles `content: ""`, drops all but one of a comma-separated selector list, and silently unwraps at-rules into unconditional declarations.

The trigger's colour, size and weight are not here either. They travel on the `core/navigation` block in `patterns/header.php`, where they are visible in the editor — Ollie's stylesheet sets `color: currentColor`, `font-size: inherit` and `font-weight: inherit` on its toggle, so the block's own attributes reach the button without help. That is the same inheritance the accordion needed a JSON declaration to restore, working correctly by default.
